title: Honeymoon Satin Slip with Lace Trim | Champagne | Bridal
description:
A bias-cut slip drapes from the diagonal, which means it moves with you instead of clinging to a straight line across the body. That difference is the whole point of a slip: it should look like fabric falling rather than fabric stretched.

The lace trim at the hem has a light scattering layer, so it is semi-sheer at the edge without being see-through across the body. The straps are convertible between straight and crisscross.

Pairs naturally with the bridal bodysuit as a wedding-night set, or stands alone as an occasion piece.

WHAT MAKES IT WORK
• Bias cut — drapes from the diagonal instead of clinging
• Lace hem with a light scattering layer, semi-sheer only at the edge
• Convertible straps: straight or crisscross
• Body is opaque; the lace is only at the hem
• Pairs with the bridal sculpting bodysuit as a set

DETAILS
• Material: 95% Acetate satin, 5% Spandex; nylon lace hem
• Color: Champagne
• Closure: Convertible adjustable straps
• Pattern: Solid with lace hem
• Origin: Made in China
• Care: Hand wash cold inside out. Line dry. Do not bleach.

FIT & SIZING
Bias cut gives more give across the body than a straight cut. Take your usual size; size down only for a closer fit.
Model is 5'7" (170 cm) with a 33" bust and 26" waist, wearing size S.

SIZING (body measurements)
Size | Bust | Underbust | Waist | Hip | Weight (lb) | Equivalent to
XS | 30–31 in | 26–27 in | 23–24 in | 33–34 in | 90–115 lb | US 0–2
S | 32–33 in | 28–29 in | 25–26 in | 35–36 in | 115–140 lb | US 4–6
M | 34–35 in | 30–31 in | 27–28 in | 37–38 in | 140–165 lb | US 8–10
L | 36–38 in | 32–34 in | 29–31 in | 39–41 in | 165–190 lb | US 12–14
XL | 39–41 in | 35–37 in | 32–34 in | 42–44 in | 190–215 lb | US 16–18

Sizing tips:
• Measure your underbust — the band directly under the bust, snug but not tight. This matters more than the bust measurement for anything with a bodysuit fit.
• Measure your hip at the widest point, roughly 8 inches below the waist. This is the number most people underestimate.
• If you are between sizes, size up for sleepwear and lounge pieces, and size down for fitted bodysuits where you want a close fit.
• Fabric stretch varies by style. Each product page lists how much give the fabric has — styles listed as "about 2 inches of stretch" will size down more easily.
• Between a standard size and an extended size? Take the standard size. The jump to extended sizing changes torso length and gusset volume, not just the measurements.

QUESTIONS WE GET A LOT
Q: What does bias cut mean here?
A: The fabric is cut on the diagonal. It drapes from the diagonal and moves with you rather than clinging along a straight line, which is what makes a slip look like a slip.

Q: Is the lace see-through?
A: The body of the slip is fully opaque. Only the lace hem is semi-sheer, and it has a light scattering layer so it does not read as transparent.

Q: Can I wear the straps crossed?
A: Yes. They are convertible — straight over the shoulders or crossed at the back, which changes the neckline and back line.

Q: Does it match the bridal bodysuit?
A: Yes, the fabric and colour are matched. Buy them together as a wedding-night set, or buy the slip on its own as an occasion piece.
